reason: Supplement specified after the grade-blind count showed 48,019 immediate rescues among 86,264 alternatives, before inspecting the first model's validation scores. Correct the selected-action denominator: did a player use a different saving move when it was available before the choice?
menu: Use all full-board-favorable opportunities of the original definition, including observed straight escapes. Enumerate every other legal move that immediately increases the original chain's liberties to at least two: such a move must capture an enemy chain adjacent to an original stone, since the only direct connection point is the single liberty. Enumerate the last liberties of adjacent enemy chains in atari, deduplicate, legally play each candidate, check the original chain and count captured stones before looking at the actual move. Report zero, one and multiple alternatives. In the unique-offer subset retain three observed categories (straight escape, the offered rescue, another move).
transfer: A conditional choice model uses the physical offer before the decision. Its immediate price proxy is stones obtainable by the alternative vs the stipulated noncapturing straight escape. No imputed engine value of unplayed outside options. Report take-up by 1, 2, 3+ stones both among all unique offers and among two-way choices.
analysis: Fit a binary conditional logistic model on folds 1/2 unique events in which one rescue is offered and the player chose it or straight escape. Base covariates: log(1+original size), 2/3+ captured stone indicators, pre-action local verdict and phase (80 and 160). Add trained grade intercepts, then grade-specific interaction slopes on log(offer size) capped at log(6). Weight training players equally within each grade and grades equally. Use fixed ridge .01 times squared coefficients (intercept free); independently fit each nested specification. Report held-out choice NLL and response probabilities, country/identity absent. For rank inference compute each hypothetical grade's observed-choice log likelihood, sum on unique games in the question, divide by sqrt(max(number of binary choices,1)), and add the two named adjacent-grade log likelihood differences to SQ4 log odds conserving each pair's mass. The common model exactly restores SQ4. Report all changes and paired player intervals. This follow-up has exploratory status; it cannot replace the primary gate. Do not retune or promote on the historical validation.
